open_points.subject: pre-parse JSON-depth measurement
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds each JSON text where it enters the kernel, measured on that text as a whole, without recursion, before anything else walks it
open_points.question: Which module owns the non-recursive raw-JSON depth scanner, and through which capability do `surface`, `installation`, `bindings`, `sandbox` and `service_invoker` use it before their parsers walk the text?
options: `canonical_values` owns one raw-text depth capability used by every entry module
Each entry module owns its own non-recursive depth scanner
The parser used by each entry module reports depth while parsing despite the stated before-parse requirement
open_points.default_guess: `canonical_values` owns one raw-text depth capability and entry-owning modules call it before parsing.

open_points.subject: mapped-output list depth
open_points.text: A13 now requires a mapped list whose canonical bytes exceed `stored_value_bytes_max`, or which nests deeper than `json_depth_max`, to fail, while `run_values` owns only “measuring every delivered list of a mapped node against `stored_value_bytes_max`” and hides only “the size measure”
open_points.question: Which module measures an assembled mapped list against `json_depth_max` and reports that failure to the run derivation?
options: `run_values` performs both byte-size and depth checks
`runs` performs the depth check after `run_values` assembles the list
open_points.default_guess: `run_values` invokes a depth check owned by `canonical_values` and returns the same list-failure result it returns for excessive size.

open_points.subject: depth limit for internally assembled identity documents
open_points.text: A01 says a value “nested deeper than `json_depth_max` … is refused where it enters”, while A20 enumerates entry texts but does not include the meaning-facts objects that `canonical_values.content_identity` assembles and canonicalises
open_points.question: Does `json_depth_max` also apply to an internally assembled contract, flow, case, value-id or other identity document when its request-carried components each satisfy the limit but their identity wrapper exceeds it; if so, which calling module owns the resulting refusal?
options: Only externally entering texts are depth-bounded; internal identity documents may be deeper
Every document passed to JCS, including internally assembled identity facts, is depth-bounded
The identity document is bounded against the release ceiling associated with its constituent stored records
open_points.default_guess: Only the explicitly enumerated entry texts are depth-bounded; internal identity wrappers are canonicalised without another depth check.

open_points.subject: non-canonical function-output byte accounting
open_points.text: The output count includes canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output — “for an output that has none, the bytes of its JSON text as returned” — although A03 defines `run` as returning Python objects, while `sandbox_runner` owns report framing and pre-counting and `sandbox` owns the deciding output count
open_points.question: What exact JSON text exists for a returned Python value that has no canonical bytes, and which module creates and reports those bytes so `sandbox` can enforce `output_bytes` deterministically?
options: `sandbox_runner` serializes every returned Python object with a specified fallback encoding and reports its byte count
`sandbox` serializes the decoded runner report and counts that representation
Only syntactically valid JSON values can reach this check, and their original JSON representation is preserved by the runner
open_points.default_guess: `sandbox_runner` owns a specified deterministic serialization of the returned object and reports its byte count to `sandbox`.
